name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Calf Raise
research: Step 0.15 m high, y -0.25..+0.05 (heel hangs off its +Y edge). Ball of the left foot fixed at B=(0.12,0.02,0.15). Rest ankle sits (0,+0.14,+0.074) from the ball; foot rot X t pivots that: t=-20 -> ankle B+(0,0.157,0.022)=(0.12,0.177,0.172), heel ~z 0.09 behind the edge (dropped); t=+35 -> ankle B+(0,0.072,0.141)=(0.12,0.092,0.291), high on the toes. Straight stance leg: pelvis = ankle + (0,0.066,0.892), shifted x +0.03 over the stance foot -> (0.03,0.243,1.064) and (0.03,0.158,1.183). Free right leg: thigh vertical under hip R, knee 80 deg, foot behind (rot X 100 = toes pointing back-down). Right hand on a wall block (inner face x -0.725) instead of a rail (no rail prop): arm elev 80, plane 10, elbow 20, hand ~0.53 m out from the shoulder at x ~-0.19 -> about x -0.72. Left hand holds the dumbbell (same side as stance leg, per library). Camera yaw +80 = his left side, so the wall is behind him and the dumbbell faces the camera. Sources: ACE wall calf raise (knee straight, hand on wall), ACE Jo 2015 (heel below the step, rise high). Facts and checks: research/single_leg_calf_raise.json.
